newsitem.title: FRANCE: Higher winter wheat sowings seen in Central France.
newsitem.headline: Higher winter wheat sowings seen in Central France.

text.p: Farmers in France's grain belt south of Paris are expected to plant more winter wheat, barley and rapeseed than in the previous season, local crop analysts said on Tuesday.
A European Union decision to halve the grain set-aside rate to five percent for the 1997 harvest was the main explanation behind the expected rise, local ONIC officials said.
"The rise results mostly from a cut in the grain set-aside rate," a local ONIC official said.
But firm wheat and barley prices in the past season among tight supplies and strong demand also encouraged farmers to plant more grain.
International world wheat prices have however recently eased under supply pressure and fierce competiton among main grain exporters.
Provisional figures established by ONIC's office in Orleans indicated winter wheat sowings may rise by some three percent to 786,000 hectares from 763,500 ha in 1996.
Winter barley sowings were seen jumping 15 percent to 150,000 hectares from 130,000.
Rapeseed sowings were put at 149,000 ha, up 9.5 percent from 136,000 ha.
Farmers should however plant less winter durum wheat because the region exceeded its maximum guaranteed area in 1996, they said. Sowings were put at 26,000 ha, down 7,000 from last season.

The region's six departments are among 24 departments excluded from a list of traditional durum wheat growing regions. As a result a maximum guaranteed area for these departments was set at 50,000 ha to be eligible for EU aid.
Local ONIC officials said autumn sowings conditions were favourable as the plants benefited from a good combination of rain and sunshine.
They cautioned figures cited were provisional and likely to be adjusted in coming weeks.
ONIC is expected to release its first official estimate for national winter grain sowings in December, ONIC officials in Paris said.
But Georges Malpel, director general of French grain growers association AGPB told Reuters the national trend was towards higher wheat, barley and rapeseed sowings.
He said soft wheat and barley sowings may rise by two to three percent over the past season.
Farm ministry figures published last week indicated farmers boosted winter wheat sowings by 5.5 percent to 4.741 million ha and barley sowings by 13.3 percent to 1.079 million ha in 1996.
Winter rapeseed sowings rose 2.4 percent to 856,000 ha while durum wheat sowings jumped 17.5 percent to 262,000 ha in 1996. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
